definitions.explanation: A large, rigid suitcase or travel case. Evokes the classic rectangular hard-sided luggage, though the word is sometimes used loosely for large bags in general.
The luggage compartment at the rear of a car. This is the standard everyday word for this part of the car in Japanese.

examples.japanese: トランクに{荷物|にもつ}を{詰|つ}める。
{革|かわ}のトランクを{持|も}って{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I set off on a trip with a leather trunk.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{古|ふる}いトランクから{戦時中|せんじちゅう}の{手紙|てがみ}が{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: Wartime letters came out of my grandfather's old trunk.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物|もの}の{袋|ふくろ}をトランクに{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put the shopping bags in the trunk.

examples.japanese: この{車|くるま}はトランクが{広|ひろ}いので、ゴルフバッグも{楽|らく}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: This car has a spacious trunk, so a golf bag fits in easily.

notes:
A loanword from English "trunk." Both senses are common in everyday Japanese.

USAGE:
For luggage, トランク evokes a traditional hard-sided rectangular case. Modern wheeled suitcases are more often called スーツケース or キャリーケース, while トランク has a somewhat classic or vintage feel in this sense. For cars, トランク is the everyday word — it works for sedans and is sometimes extended to SUVs and hatchbacks, though {荷室|にしつ} (cargo area) is also used for those.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- トランクを{開|あ}ける: to open the trunk
- トランクに{積|つ}む: to load into the trunk
- トランクルーム: storage room, trunk room (a rental storage unit)
- トランクス: boxer shorts (trunks — note the different word)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スーツケース: suitcase — the standard modern word for wheeled luggage
- キャリーケース: carry-on case — wheeled luggage, especially cabin-size
- {荷室|にしつ}: cargo area — a more generic term for a vehicle's luggage space
